title: AI papers — arXiv announcement batch, 17 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This ordering is inferred from checkable external coverage, project releases, cross-list breadth, and reported evaluations; recent-paper citation evidence is limited, and the external signals are weak proxies rather than readership or download counts.

sections.title: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
sections.abstract: The authors train visual agents on contrast sets of high-resolution images so success requires inspecting the changed evidence, reporting 63.3% set accuracy versus 59.3% for GRPO at maximum resolution.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce CrossRPO, a group-relative policy objective over image contrast sets, and release ViRA-Train, ViRA-Bench, and ViRA-Bench-Real; their reported comparison is on the stated benchmark suite.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note that ViRA-Bench-Real contains only 78 photographed sets, shot indoors with one camera, and that the training/evaluation base models come from one model family.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in vision and AI; public project repository, Hugging Face Papers discussion page, and separate technical summary provide checkable corroboration, not readership counts.

sections.title: SciResearch-Eval: Evaluating Scientific Judgment in Autonomous Experimental Agents
sections.abstract: This paper presents an interactive thermal-measurement benchmark in which agents design experiments, reason with a potentially flawed simulator, and report calibrated intervals against exact ground truth; the authors report confident miscalibration on many simulator-mismatch tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute a benchmark combining agent-designed experiments, deliberately flawed simulators, and proper interval scoring against exact simulated truth, with a held-out evaluation of nine models.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly describe the benchmark as one physical domain by design; transfer to other scientific domains remains to be tested.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed across AI, ML, and computational physics; a public benchmark repository and a distinct technical paper summary provide checkable project and cross-category signals.

sections.title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
sections.abstract: ScaleVLA connects a 552B vision-language backbone to a trainable action diffusion transformer and reports gains over smaller backbones in simulation sample efficiency, generalization, and a small real-world charger-insertion evaluation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a controlled 2B-to-552B backbone comparison with fixed action-side setup, plus simulation and real-robot results; their real-robot in-domain charger insertion result is 9/10 versus 4/10 for the 2B baseline.
sections.unique_caveat: Each trained policy uses one training seed, and the real-robot in-domain result is based on ten trials; the paper also notes the 552B model requires more hardware than smaller backbones.
sections.ranking_evidence: A project page, Hugging Face Papers page, and separate coverage from AI Weekly and ExplainX corroborate attention to the robotics experiment; this does not establish adoption or replication.

sections.title: Jetriever: Shifting Agent Memory Retrieval from Similarity to Utility
sections.abstract: Jetriever ranks stored memories by estimated usefulness to the current question rather than text similarity, reporting that it places the gold exchange first in 84.8% of 125 indirect-query tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors replace similarity search with full-pool utility scoring and report matched retrieval comparisons on InMind plus a sampled MemoryAgentBench evaluation.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that full-pool scoring grows with the memory store; the principal indirect-query result is based on 125 tasks, so broader and longer-running memory evaluations remain open.
sections.ranking_evidence: Separate Grafy and KBLIP technical coverage surfaced the paper; these are discussion signals, not independent replications.

sections.title: Latent Lattice Language Models
sections.abstract: The paper adds persistent per-layer latent streams that condition attention, cache writes, and MLP computation, reporting lower validation perplexity than a parameter-matched Transformer in its 406M-parameter, 20B-token experiment.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce the Lattice of Latents as a companion set of persistent per-layer computational states and report gains across Transformer and recurrent-backbone experiments.
sections.unique_caveat: The headline parameter-matched language-model result is for a 406M model trained on 20B FineWeb-Edu tokens; the paper's evidence does not by itself establish how the gains scale to larger training runs or downstream deployments.
sections.ranking_evidence: The paper spans three core AI categories and received independently hosted technical explainers, including DeepPaper and Foorilla; the signal is breadth of public discussion, not measured citation or usage growth.
